learning: Check whether slalom completion_time falls below 2.2 s, whether s-bend steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.36, whether any run goes off_track, and whether line_loss_events stay near 1 per run. If oscillation rises, kd needs about 0.70 to offset the 10% higher turn rate.
notes: Single-variable step from iteration 8: wheel_radius 0.040 to 0.044 m, with the controller and all other geometry unchanged. Full measurement set requested so the wheel effect on completion_time and oscillation can be read directly.
rationale: Iteration 8 (best so far, 939.3) finished 60/60 with rms_error 0.0056 to 0.0099 m, slalom completion_time about 2.26 s, and line_loss_events about 1 per run. Iteration 9 showed that sensor_size 0.016 m cut s-bend line loss but caused 4 slalom off_track endings, so I keep sensor_size 0.012 m, as the Builder's intent specifies. The Builder's single-variable step raises wheel_radius from 0.040 to 0.044 m. Ground speed rises about 10% at the same PWM, and turn rate per unit wheel differential rises about 10% too. Iteration 8 had margin on oval and slalom, and s-bend steering_oscillation was 0.34, so the main risk is oscillation rising on the s-bend. I deliberately keep the iteration 8 controller unchanged (kp 3.8, ki 0.15, kd 0.65, base_speed 1.4, last_direction line loss, weights x/0.015). That keeps the wheel-radius effect readable, and the Builder's intent expects the controller to carry over. ki 0.15 still cancels the fixed motor mismatch. Expected, not claimed: completion_time falls by about 0.1 to 0.2 s on slalom and oval, completions stay 60/60, and line_loss_events stay near 1. If s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.36 in the next race, the next controller step is kd about 0.70.
